Rob Sand

Democratic candidate for Governor and Lieutenant Governor, Iowa · Open seat

Iowa State Auditor; attorney

Rob Sand has been Iowa's State Auditor since January 2019. Before that he was an Iowa assistant attorney general from 2010 to 2017. He had no opponent in the Democratic primary and is the Democratic nominee for governor, with Crawford County farmer Dave Muhlbauer as his running mate, for the seat Gov. Kim Reynolds is leaving.

Where Sand stands

K-12 education funding
Promises a 5% increase in State Supplemental Aid for K-12 schools in his first year as governor. Says he can't promise that level in year two because of the state budget deficit.
Taxes and state budget
Wants to end tax deals for data centers and legalize cannabis and tax it like alcohol to fund priorities. Says cannabis would bring in about $50 million in year one and more than $100 million in later years.
Cannabis
Supports legalizing cannabis and regulating it like alcohol.
School lunch
Supports free school lunch. Says paying for it depends on closing the budget deficit and finding new revenue.
Water quality and cancer
Proposes a cabinet-level task force on Iowa's cancer rates. Also proposes income and property tax credits for farmers who adopt water-quality practices.
Medicaid
Pledges to end Iowa's privatized Medicaid system right away.
Abortion
Opposes Iowa's six-week abortion ban. Says he would veto any further limits on reproductive care, including IVF, surrogacy and contraception, and acknowledges he could not repeal the ban on his own.
Government accountability
Proposes term and age limits for elected officials, a ban on stock trading by officeholders, required public town halls and an open primary.
Social policy legislation
Says he would veto future "culture war bills" and focus state government on water quality, cancer, the economy, education and health care.
Bipartisanship
Says his cabinet would be "tripartisan" and that he expects to govern alongside a Republican-controlled legislature.
